title: Session 49: Implementation-lug review/reconciliation workflow canonicalized
description: Successfully canonicalized the implementation-lug review/reconciliation workflow by extending the object model, updating canonical guidance, and establishing durable review patterns. This turns the observed review trail from implementation-canonical-runtime-baseline-v1 into first-class behavior for all implementation lugs.
accomplished: Extended implementation-lug object model with review_notes[], review_cycles[], acceptance fields
Added lifecycle/status support for review states: planned → review_pending → approved_to_implement → in_progress → in_remediation → ready_for_recheck → implemented → accepted
Updated canonical guidance in templates/commands/wai-lug-advisor.md and WAI-Spoke/reference/auto/wai-lug-advisor.md
Updated implementation-canonical-runtime-baseline-v1 with new fields, real review note for WAI-Signals.jsonl references, and status reflecting remediation reality
Created implementation-lug-review-workflow-v1 as planning/control lug with complete review cycle example
Created task-lug-storage-cleanup-v1 for future backup file rescue
decisions: Established canonical review/reconciliation workflow for implementation lugs
Made review notes persistent in lug objects, not just chat
Added comprehensive lifecycle states supporting remediation cycles
Extended object model additively to preserve backward readability
Used implementation-canonical-runtime-baseline-v1 as concrete example with real review issue
verification_performed: Confirmed canonical guidance describes review-note/remediation workflow in both template and WAI-Spoke versions
Confirmed implementation-canonical-runtime-baseline-v1 carries new review/remediation fields with actual review note
Confirmed active example lug reflects remediation reality (in_remediation status) not false acceptance
Confirmed workflow is understandable from files alone without chat context
Verified 137+ WAI-Signals.jsonl references documented as blocking review note
workflow_changes: Review notes must be persistent in lug objects
Review cycles track each review pass with model attribution
Open review notes prevent final acceptance
Remediation workflow: gap found → in_remediation → fix → ready_for_recheck → re-review → accepted
Model attribution required for all review activities
implementation_approach: Used the observed pattern from implementation-canonical-runtime-baseline-v1 as the canonical template, then applied it back to that same lug as the first concrete example
follow_up_work: Test new workflow with future implementation lugs
Consider applying review patterns to other high-impact lug types
canonical_alignment: All changes extend canonical design by making review trails durable and independent of chat context
